My current theory on what is going on with Freedom Six Wraith.

With the announcement of Sentinel Tactics: Battle For Broken City, we saw 5 Spite clones. We also learned that with the damages done to Rook City thanks to Deadline and Progeny, there were some issues with The Chairman's under ground facility that resulted in many of the clones not surviving. We know Deadline went to Earth to cause mass destruction to try and lure away OblivAeon. However, Iron legacy seems to have done that in his timeline, resulting in Deadline not taking notice of the planet. It also seems as though there is one OblivAeon that exist, traveling where and when as he pleases. Sincet the main timeline is the one he is more interested in, the Iron Legacy's timeline planet may not have a Progeny. Due to Deadline and Progeny possibly not attacking in the Iron legacy Timeline, it is likely that a lot more of the Spite clones could have survived. Perhaps The Wraith or Iron legacy instead initiated the reasoning as to why The Chairman went into hiding in his underground facility. 

We have no confirmation as to whether or not Freedom Six Wraith's artwork takes place prior to or after the final conflict with Iron Legacy. Going with that it is actually after the battle, then perhaps this is after The Chairman has come back, bringing even more Spite clones with him than he does in the main timeline. One of the first things he decides to do is to take out The Wraith, as she has taken over for him while he was away.

posts.name: waedens
posts.cooked: I just think that this is how Christopher tells stories. No offense to Christopher, but he is not a great novelist. If he was, he would write a book. Instead he is a game designer. He has all the elements of the plot and the overarching story he wants to tell, but his talent is not writing it all down giving the characters the dialog that delivers the intensity that they deserve. So, through Adam he paints snap shots of important moments that fit with the plot that he wants to advance. He then leaves it to our imagination to fill in the details. It is actually a classical way of telling a story taken to the extreme. When Homer wrote that Helen of Troy was the most beautiful woman in the world he did not then describe her. By leaving Helen a blank canvas we can all imagine our own version of idea beauty. Yours will be different than mine. I believe that the same kind of thing is happening here. Of the whole Kickstarter I am most worried about the comic because I think it will be hard for it to live up to what we hope it will be…
